```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
library(broom)
```

# Part 1 — Data Loading and Preprocessing

## 1.1 Load data and inspect missingness

```{r load}
df <- read.csv("./user-level-df.csv")

# FIX #3: report how many rows are lost to drop_na() before dropping,
# so we know whether missingness is negligible or systematic.
n_before <- nrow(df)
df <- df %>% drop_na()
n_after <- nrow(df)

cat("Rows before drop_na():", n_before, "\n")
cat("Rows after drop_na(): ", n_after, "\n")
cat("Rows dropped:         ", n_before - n_after,
    sprintf("(%.2f%%)", 100 * (n_before - n_after) / n_before), "\n")
```

## 1.2 Prepare covariates

The data remain in start-stop (counting-process) form: each row represents one
monthly risk interval. This allows the covariates, and their hazard ratios, to
vary over time without treating the rows as independent survival records.

Skewed covariates (`betweenness`, `mean_degree`, `effective_topics`) are
log1p-transformed first, then all covariates are z-score standardized.
Note: standardization is computed over all user-month rows, so long spells
contribute more observations to the mean/sd (documented in Methods).

```{r covariates}
COVARIATES <- c(
  "mean_degree", "betweenness", "semantic_dispersion", "effective_topics"
)

df_clean <- df %>%
  mutate(
    betweenness      = log1p(betweenness),
    mean_degree      = log1p(mean_degree),
    #effective_topics = log1p(effective_topics),
    #semantic_dispersion = log1p(semantic_dispersion)
  ) %>%
  # Z-score normalize (after log transforms)
  mutate(across(all_of(COVARIATES), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))

head(df_clean)
```

## 1.3 Sanity check — risk-set integrity (FIX #2)

Once a user adopts a term (event == 1), they must exit the risk set: no
subsequent rows should exist for that user-term-subreddit-spell. This chunk
verifies that, and removes any post-adoption rows if found.

```{r risk-set-check}
post_adoption_rows <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(user, term, subreddit, spell_id) %>%
  filter(any(event == 1)) %>%
  mutate(first_event_stop = min(stop[event == 1])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(start >= first_event_stop)

cat("Rows occurring after adoption:", nrow(post_adoption_rows), "\n")

# If any post-adoption rows exist, remove them so users exit the risk set
# at adoption. (If spells are intentionally recurrent, revisit this choice
# and the clustering structure instead of deleting rows.)
if (nrow(post_adoption_rows) > 0) {
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    group_by(user, term, subreddit, spell_id) %>%
    mutate(first_event_stop = if (any(event == 1)) min(stop[event == 1]) else Inf) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(start < first_event_stop) %>%
    select(-first_event_stop)
  cat("Post-adoption rows removed. Remaining rows:", nrow(df_clean), "\n")
}
```

## 1.4 Descriptives of adoption times

```{r adoption-times}
adoption_times <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(user, term, subreddit, spell_id) %>%
  summarise(
    adopted = any(event == 1),
    adoption_time = if_else(adopted, min(stop[event == 1]), NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

adoption_times %>%
  filter(adopted) %>%
  summarise(
    n_adoptions          = n(),
    mean_adoption_time   = mean(adoption_time),
    median_adoption_time = median(adoption_time),
    sd_adoption_time     = sd(adoption_time)
  )
```

```{r summary}
summary(df_clean)
```

# Part 2 — Main Cox model

```{r main-model}
fit <- coxph(
  Surv(start, stop, event) ~
    mean_degree +
    betweenness +
    semantic_dispersion +
    effective_topics,
  cluster = user,
  data = df_clean
)

summary(fit)
tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)  # hazard ratios
```

## 2.1 Proportional hazards check

```{r zph}
my_zph <- cox.zph(fit)
my_zph
```

# Part 3 — Time-varying effect model (FIX #1)

Because the data are already in counting-process form, we do NOT use `tt()`.
Instead we construct the time interaction explicitly as an ordinary covariate:
each row's interval endpoint (`stop`) provides the time value, so
`betweenness * log(stop)` implements the same hypothesis as
`tt(x) = x * log(t)` but is fully supported for start-stop data and
reproducible. Only betweenness receives the interaction, since the PH
violation for mean_degree was resolved by the log transform.

```{r time-varying-model}
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(betweenness_x_logt = betweenness * log(stop)) %>%
  mutate(degree_x_logt = mean_degree * log(stop))

fit_nonph <- coxph(
  Surv(start, stop, event) ~
    mean_degree +
    betweenness +
    betweenness_x_logt +
    degree_x_logt + 
    semantic_dispersion +
    effective_topics,
  cluster = user,
  data = df_clean
)

summary(fit_nonph)
tidy(fit_nonph, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)  # hazard ratios
```

# Part 4 — Robustness: stratified models

These models absorb all term-level and subreddit-level heterogeneity into
stratum-specific baseline hazards. Semantic features are constant within a
term, so they are only estimable in the unstratified models above; the
stratified network model shows that network effects hold even after
controlling for all slang- and community-level differences.

## 4.1 Network features only, strata(term, subreddit)

```{r network-strata}
fit_network <- coxph(
  Surv(start, stop, event) ~
    mean_degree + betweenness + strata(term, subreddit),
  cluster = user,
  data = df_clean
)

summary(fit_network)
tidy(fit_network, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

```{r network-strata-zph}
cox.zph(fit_network)
```

## 4.2 Linguistic features only, strata(subreddit)

Note: `strata(term)` would absorb the semantic features entirely (they are
constant within each term), so the linguistic robustness model stratifies by
subreddit only.

```{r linguistic-strata}
fit_linguistic <- coxph(
  Surv(start, stop, event) ~
    semantic_dispersion + effective_topics + strata(subreddit),
  cluster = user,
  data = df_clean
)

summary(fit_linguistic)
tidy(fit_linguistic, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```
